rules.name: Virtual environment
rules.what: A virtual environment with this project's installed packages. The project lists its dependencies, so it can be recreated.
rules.comeback: Recreate it from the project's requirements (for example uv sync, poetry install, or python -m venv .venv then pip install -r requirements.txt).

rules.name: Virtual environment (no requirements file)
rules.what: A virtual environment with no requirements file next to it, so Leftover can't tell how to rebuild it. If the folder it belongs to is gone, it may be an orphan.
rules.comeback: Before removing it, save its package list with pip freeze so you can recreate it.

rules.name: __pycache__
rules.what: Compiled bytecode Python writes next to your source files to start faster.
rules.comeback: Python writes it again automatically the next time the code runs.

rules.name: Test and lint caches
rules.what: Caches pytest, mypy and Ruff keep between runs.
rules.comeback: Each tool rebuilds its cache on its next run.

rules.name: .tox
rules.what: Environments tox creates to run your tests against different setups.
rules.comeback: tox recreates them on its next run.

rules.name: pip cache
rules.what: Wheels and downloads pip keeps to make installs faster.
rules.comeback: pip downloads packages again when it needs them.

rules.name: uv cache
rules.what: Packages, wheels and Python builds uv has downloaded.
rules.comeback: uv downloads what it needs again on the next sync or install.

rules.name: Poetry cache
rules.what: Package metadata and downloaded files Poetry keeps between installs.
rules.comeback: Poetry downloads them again on the next install.

rules.name: Conda package cache
rules.what: Downloaded conda packages. Some may be hard-linked into your environments, so conda's own clean command is the safe way to shrink it.
rules.comeback: conda clean only removes packages no environment is using.

rules.name: Conda environments
rules.what: Your conda environments. Each one can hold packages you installed by hand, so Leftover never touches them.
